title: Tobacco, coffee and tea as global commodities
summary: Coffee, tea, cocoa, tobacco and sugar are counted among the first modern commodities. In Virginia, John Rolfe was growing Spanish-type tobacco by 1612, and by 1615-16 the colony was shipping it to England, saving its economy. Coffee, monopolised by Yemen until the Dutch began growing it on Java at the end of the 1600s, spread to the Caribbean and Latin America on slave plantations. In North America it went from a luxury in the seventeenth century to a mass drink by the mid-nineteenth, rivalling tea.

uncertainty.note: From early 17th-century commercial tobacco (Rolfe, 1612) to coffee becoming a mass drink by the mid-19th century (Topik and McDonald).

as_recorded.value: from luxury beverage in the seventeenth century to mass consumer drink by the mid-nineteenth century

The emergence of coffeehouses and retail tea transforms urban European sociability and spurs maritime commodity imports.
